result.topic_en: Euler reduces the impossibility of $a^5+b^5$ being a fifth power and of $a^3+b^3=c^3$ to statements about squares of the form $x^6-4xy^5$ and $x^4-4xy^3$, studies the cubic $x^3+(x+a)^3=(x+b)^3$ by bounding the roots of $y^3=\alpha yy+\beta y+\gamma$, and begins a problem on making $x^3+ny^3$ a square.
result.transcription:
232 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
$\frac{z^5}{x^5}$, seu $\frac{xz^5}{x^6}$, ita ut foret $\frac{xx-yy}{4xx}=\frac{xz^5}{x^6}$;
multiplicetur per $4x^6$, fietque
$x^6-x^4yy=4xz^5$, sive $x^6-4xz^5=x^4yy=\Box$.
Quare si demonstrari posset formulam $x^6-4xy^5$ quadratum esse non posse, simul demonstratum est formulam $a^5+b^5$ potestatem quintam esse non posse. Si enim esset $x^6-4xy^5$ quadratum; ob factores $x(x^5-4y^5)$ inter se primos, uterque quadratum esse deberet. Sit igitur $x=pp$, et alter factor $p^{10}-4y^5$ deberet esse quadratum, puta $qq$; foret ergo
$p^{10}-qq=4y^5=4r^5s^5=(p^5+q)(p^5-q)$, ideoque $p^5+q=2r^5$ et $p^5-q=2s^5$,
unde addendo foret $2p^5=2r^5+2s^5$, sive $p^5=r^5+s^5$.
Simili modo formula $a^3+b^3=c^3$ transformabitur in hanc aequivalentem $x^4-4xy^3=\Box$. Hoc postremum theorema etiam hoc modo repraesentari potest, ut nunquam fieri queat
$x^3+(x+a)^3=(x+b)^3$, ubi manifesto $b>a$.
Foret ergo $x^3=(x+b)^3-(x+a)^3=3(b-a)xx+3(bb-aa)x+b^3-a^3$,
demonstrandum ergo est hanc aequationem nunquam habere radicem rationalem. Ad hoc observetur, cum posterius membrum factorem habeat $b-a$, etiam $x^3$ talem factorem habere debet, et perspicuum est $b-a$ vel esse cubum, vel noncuplum cubi.
Sit primo $b-a=f^3$, et erit $x^3=3f^3xx+3f^3(b+a)x+f^3(bb+ab+aa)$.
Ponatur ergo $x=fy$, eritque $y^3=3ffyy+3(b+a)fy+bb+ab+aa$, ideoque $y$ debet esse factor formulae $bb+ab+aa$.
Sit secundo $b-a=9f^3$, et ultimum membrum fieret (ob $b=9f^3+a$)
$9^3f^9+3.9^2af^6+3.9aaf^3=27f^3(27f^6+9af^3+aa)$,
unde fit $x^3=27f^3xx+27f^3(b+a)x+27f^3(27f^6+9af^3+aa)$.
Ponatur $x=3fy$, erit $y^3=9ffyy+3fy(b+a)+27f^6+9af^3+aa$.
Pro utroque casu limites assignari possunt; pro priore enim manifesto est $y>3ff$, et pro altero $y>9ff$, qui limites sunt nimis parvi; nimis magni autem hoc modo reperientur: Consideretur aequatio in genere
$y^3=\alpha yy+\beta y+\gamma$,
ubi $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ sint positivi, ac primo erit $y>\alpha$; deinde cum sit $y=\alpha+\frac{\beta}{y}+\frac{\gamma}{yy}$, si in membro posteriori loco $y$ scribatur $\alpha$, hoc membrum fit nimis magnum, erit ergo $y<\alpha+\frac{\beta}{\alpha}+\frac{\gamma}{\alpha\alpha}$; ponatur hic limes $=\lambda$, ut sit $y<\lambda$, eritque vicissim $y=\alpha+\frac{\beta}{\lambda}+\frac{\gamma}{\lambda\lambda}$.
Exemplum. Sit pro casu priori $f=1$ et $a=1$, erit $b=2$ et $x=y$, hinc $y^3=3yy+9y+7$, ubi statim $y>3$, hinc $y<7$, hinc $y>4\frac{3}{7}$, $y<5\frac{12}{31}$, radix ergo rationalis deberet esse 5, quae cum non sit divisor ultimi termini . . . . . .

Problema. Invenire numeros $x$ et $y$ inter se primos, ut formula $x^3+ny^3$ fiat numerus quadratus.
Solutio. Si hi numeri non essent primi inter se, quaestio foret levissima; posito enim $x=pr$ et $y=qr$, formula nostra prodit $r^3(p^3+nq^3)$, quae aequetur quadrato $r^4ss$, ita ut hinc statim fiat
$r=\frac{p^3+nq^3}{ss}$, unde fit $x=\frac{p^4+npq^3}{ss}$ et $y=\frac{p^3q+nq^4}{ss}$.

methods.what: Reduction of $a^5+b^5=c^5$ to the formula $x^6-4xy^5$ being a square
Descent: if $x^6-4xy^5$ is a square then coprime factors give $p^5=r^5+s^5$

items.quote: Quare si demonstrari posset formulam $x^6-4xy^5$ quadratum esse non posse, simul demonstratum est formulam $a^5+b^5$ potestatem quintam esse non posse.
items.english: Therefore if it could be proved that the formula $x^6-4xy^5$ cannot be a square, it would at the same time be proved that the formula $a^5+b^5$ cannot be a fifth power.

items.quote: demonstrandum ergo est hanc aequationem nunquam habere radicem rationalem.
items.english: It must therefore be proved that this equation never has a rational root.

items.quote: perspicuum est $b-a$ vel esse cubum, vel noncuplum cubi.
items.english: it is clear that $b-a$ is either a cube or nine times a cube.

items.quote: radix ergo rationalis deberet esse 5, quae cum non sit divisor ultimi termini . . . . . .
items.english: the rational root would therefore have to be 5, which, since it is not a divisor of the last term . . . . . .

items.quote: Problema. Invenire numeros $x$ et $y$ inter se primos, ut formula $x^3+ny^3$ fiat numerus quadratus.
items.english: Problem. To find numbers $x$ and $y$, coprime to each other, such that the formula $x^3+ny^3$ becomes a square number.
